audits.derivedAnswer: A: 367. The least entry is 157 and the greatest is 210.
audits.mathematicalReason: Use coordinates centered at 1, with x increasing rightward and y upward. Ring k ends at its upper-right corner (k,k) with value (2k+1)². The second row from the top has y=6. Its entries for x=-6 through 6 are 157 through 169, since 13²-12=157. The outer-ring entries at x=-7 and x=7 are respectively 15²-15=210 and 13²+1=170. Thus the requested sum is 157+210=367. The square-layer formulas provide a valid application of representing a visual pattern algebraically.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the cube edge length be s>0. Each section side is a face-triangle hypotenuse with legs s and s/2, so all four sides have length s√5/2. Thus EJCI is a rhombus. Its diagonal EC is a cube body diagonal of length s√3. Its other diagonal JI joins opposite vertical-edge midpoints at the same height and has length s√2. The section area is therefore (s√3)(s√2)/2=s²√6/2. Dividing by face area s² and squaring gives R²=3/2. The proposed rhombus and Pythagorean route is valid, with rhombus recognition and cube structure supplying the stated support.

audits.mathematicalReason: The diameter is FE=9+16+9=34, so its radius is 17. Its midpoint O is also the midpoint of DA, giving OA=8. audits.mathematicalReason: Let every hexagon side have length s>0. Joining B, D, and F partitions the depicted hexagon into central triangle BDF and triangles ABF, BCD, and DEF. The latter three are congruent by SAS, each with equal sides s enclosing 30°, so BDF is equilateral. Dropping a perpendicular to one of the length-s sides of a lobe gives height s/2, hence lobe area s²/4. The same 30° right triangle and Pythagoras give BF²=(2-√3)s². Consequently, the central triangle has area √3(2-√3)s²/4. The total is 3s²/4+√3(2-√3)s²/4=√3s²/2. Equating this to 6√3 yields s²=12, so the perimeter is 6s=12√3. This validates the composite-area and equilateral-triangle scopes without assuming visual symmetry.

audits.mathematicalReason: Place AD on y=0 and take F=(0,1). Then E=(-2,1), G=(2,1), and the large circle has radius 2. Above EG, the shaded region is a large semicircle of area 2π. Between EG and AD, the two shaded gaps are the portions of the 4-by-1 rectangle outside one full small semicircle and two quarter-circles; their area is 4-π. Adding gives 7π/3-√3+4, so (a,b,c,d)=(7,3,3,4) and their sum is 17. The proposed sector-minus-triangle method and supporting scopes are defensible.
